courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: General Psychology

meetings.location: Fung King Hey Bldg Swire Hall1
Fung King Hey Bldg Swire Hall1
Fung King Hey Bldg Swire Hall1
Fung King Hey Bldg Swire Hall1

courses.description: A broad-based introduction to the study of behaviour and mental processes. This course is suitable for students who might be interested in taking further courses in psychology. Topics include learning, development, psychotherapy, the brain and states of consciousness, sensation and perception, memory, social behaviour, personality, psychological disorders, coping and health, stress, and others.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
Not for students who have obtained the following grade in Psychology: IB - 5 or above (HL)/GCE-AL - C or above (AL)/Cambridge Pre-U - P2 or above (Principal course)/HKALE - C or above (AL)/AP Exam - 3 or above. 
Not for students who have taken UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, you will be expected to
I. Demonstrate a basic understanding in various areas of psychology (matches with Learning Goal I)
II. Relate and apply major psychological concepts and theories in analyzing real-life situations (matches with Learning Goal I, II, III)
III. Conceptualize, structure, and express personal views, both in written and verbal formats, on various topics of psychology
(matches with Learning Goal I, II, III, IV)
IV. Develop insights about human behavior and mental processes (matches with Learning Goal I, II, III, IV)

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Positive Psychology in Everyday Life
courses.description:
(UGED1554 is double-coded with PSYC1020.)
Positive psychology is the scientific study of positive influences in life, namely, positive subjective experiences, positive individual traits, and positive institutions that enhance our quality of life and avert pathologies in time of adversities. This is a knowledge-based course introducing the basic concepts of positive psychology and its application in daily life. This course aims at inspiring students’ interest and self-reflection in positive psychology, as well as the healthy mindsets and lifestyles that it espouses, while encouraging students to plan and initiate habit changes via the integration of positive psychology in their daily lives.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken UGED1553 and UGED1554.
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students should be able to:

* Understand the scientific foundation of positive psychology
* Recognize the empirically validated practices that enhance individual well-being
* Obtain knowledge about the real life applications of positive psychology in different settings, e.g., educational and business organizations
* Reflect on personal experiences using positive psychological concepts
* Plan self-improvement habit changes via integration of positive psychology in their daily lives

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Personal Growth

meetings.location: Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G02
Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G02
Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G02

courses.description: This course aims at providing knowledge about adjustment and personal growth to enable students to develop more effective coping skills and social behaviours. Topics include models of personality, life cycle, self-identity, love and attraction, sexual knowledge and fulfilment, marriage and family, life style and health, stress management, social skills training, assertiveness training and theories on competent personhood.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken UGED2591, UGED1600/SOWK1150 or SOWK1113.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, you will be expected to

I. Demonstrate a fundamental understanding in various areas of personal growth

II. Relate and apply major psychological concepts and theories in analyzing real-life situations

III. Conceptualize and express personal views, both in written and verbal formats, on various topics of personal growth

IV. Gain insights about your personal development and life experience

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Your Journey into Psychology
courses.description: This course offers an orientation to help beginning students of psychology to appreciate the impact of studying psychology. Students and the teacher will explore and reflect on issues including how psychology relates to oneself, how psychologists think, and how psychology contributes to the society.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken PSYC1090.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Reflecting on how the study of psychology relates to personal life and world issues
2. Appreciating the perspectives and tools of a psychologist
3. Exploring the various paths followed by students of psychology.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Introduction to Statistics
courses.description: Introduction to statistics as a method in describing and making inferences about numerical data. Emphasis on applications in daily life and psychological research.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken COMM3110, DSME2011, ECON2121, GRMD2102, LING3403, PHPC2015, SEEM2430, SOCI2004, SPED2600, STAT2101, 2102, 2001 or 2006.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students will know the procedure to carry out statistical methods in psychology and be able to both use them in practical question and understand them in the scientific literature.
2. Students will understand the logic behind those procedures and know how to solve similar questions.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Experimental Design
courses.description: Introduction to the various strategies and techniques of experimental research and data analysis employed in psychology. Participation in laboratories or independent research required.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students will know the basic types of experimental designs (e.g., within-subjects designs vs. between-subjects designs) and know how to use them appropriately in various situations.

2. Students will know how to address the important issues in designing and conducting psychological experiments (e.g., research ethics, literature review, control groups, presentations).

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychological Testing
courses.description: Basic principles of psychological measurement. Scaling models based on psychophysical and psychological methods, including constant methods, pair-comparisons, rank order, interval and ratio judgements. Issues in internal structure of measures such as variance and covariance, measurement error, and validity and reliability.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC2010 or any of its equivalent courses (COMM3110, DSME2010 & 2020, ECON2121, GRMD2102, SEEM2430, SOCI1004, SPED2600, STAT2101 & 2102, or STAT2001 & 2006).
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon completion of this course, you will have a better understanding about the basic concepts and principles of psychological testing. In particular, you will know how to evaluate the quality of a psychological test scientifically.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Qualitative Research Methods

meetings.location: Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G02
Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G02

courses.description: This course introduces students to the methods of doing qualitative research in psychology. We will begin by discussing qualitative research as a general research strategy and work through several interrelated methods of collecting qualitative data: unstructured observations, structured observations, interviews (again, varying in range from completely open-ended to more directed), diaries, and public expressions. In addition, we will discuss how to design are search project that involves qualitative methods, as well as several methods for collecting, analysing, interpreting, and writing up reports based on qualitative data. Students will be given hands-on exercises in collecting interview and observational data and will be expected to transcribe audio and/or video-recordings that they make and take field notes of their experiences.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. understand, relate and apply the key qualitative research concepts in daily circumstances

2. familiarize with the key classical and contemporary qualitative research methods in psychology

3. conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during tutorial discussions, on research methods related topics

4. design, direct and regulate group project for problem-based learning, from collecting observation data, interviewing, coding, report writing and presentation, reflecting on what have been learnt, to applying the knowledge to future problems

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Physiological Psychology
courses.description: The biological bases of behaviour, including central nervous system, peripheral nervous system, and the internal chemical environment. The relationship between such psychological processes as motivation, states of consciousness, memory, emotions,and learning and underlying physiological and neurophysiological events.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to achieve:

1. Understand major concepts and research findings in each major aspects of physiological psychology, and integrate knowledge for the human nervous system to form an overall impression of how it functions as unified system.

2. Be able to comprehend and assess recent research progress in selected research areas in brain sciences.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Sensation and Perception
courses.description: This course covers fundamental concepts and principles of sensory and perceptual processes, with an emphasis on psychophysical and scaling methods and experimental techniques. Contents include: psychophysics and scaling, sensory systems, perceptual development, constancies and illusions, and attention.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: (PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581) and PSYC2010 or its equivalent courses (COMM3110, DSME2010 & 2020, ECON2121, GRMD2102, SEEM2430, SOCI1004, SPED2600, STAT2101 & 2102 or STAT2001 & 2006).
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understanding the processes of creating perception from sensory stimuli, focusing on an approach of information processing.

2. Understanding perception from a few aspects, what is its functional goal, How is it implemented, what are the important sub-systems and how do they behave.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Basic Learning Processes
courses.description: Methods and findings in the study of learning with emphasis on their relation to theories of learning. Special consideration given to the way in which learning theory may be applied to human behaviour. Some laboratory participation required.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
The above three learning goals focusing on understanding, critical thinking, and application translate specifically to the following concrete learning outcomes:
1. Students are able to explain to others what learning, memory, and behaviorism are.
2. Students are able to discuss some basic principles governing learning and memory behavior in an informative fashion.
3. Students are able to develop sensible arguments that are based upon these principles and apply them effectively to daily life observations.
4. Students can apply these principles to some other areas of psychology and even other branches of social science.
5. Students can analyze and discuss educational issues in an informative fashion.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Memory and Cognition
courses.description: This course introduces basic concepts, theories, methods, findings, and new developments in the cognitive study of human memory. Topics to be covered include sensory memory, attention, pattern recognition, memory and forgetting, picture memory, and mental imagery.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
1. Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
2. Not for students who have taken UGEB2721 or LING2201.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon successful completion of this course, you should be able to:

1) Understand the major concepts, findings, and theories in cognitive psychology

2) Be able to understand and compare cognitive theories on different topics

3) Obtain skills and experience in conducting research in cognitive psychology

4) Develop critical thinking skills to evaluate empirical evidence

5) Practice on effective communication through written and oral presentation

6) Apply the knowledge about cognition to enhance performance in daily life

7) Appreciate the values of cognitive psychology

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: The goal of this course is to introduce students to the field of developmental psychology. We will explore theories, research methods, and research findings concerning physical, cognitive, and psychosocial development from infancy to old age. We will pay particular attention to the role of culture in shaping lifespan development.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
Pre-requisite:PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
Not for students who have taken PSYC2530 or PSYC3540 or SOWK2110 or EDUC2310.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Obtain a knowledge base of developmental psychology

2. Apply major concepts, theories, and research findings in developmental psychology to analyze real-life issues

3. Understand typical research methods in developmental psychology and practice using them

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: Major concepts and methods used in studying the individual's behaviour in social settings. Interpersonal attraction, leadership, aggression, group processes, attitude change and person perception.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerepuisite: PSYC1000 or PSYC1620 or PSYC1630 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Understand concepts and theories in social psychology.

Understand how research in social psychology is conducted.

Apply social psychology to everyday life.

Effectively communicate issues relevant to social psychology.

Develop insight into your own and others’ social behaviors.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Personality Psychology
courses.description: This course presents the major theoretical approaches to personality and the basic techniques utilized to assess personality differences. The focus is on everyday life applications, empirical evidence in support and against the theories, and the design, application, and interpretation of personality questionnaires.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1: familiarize with the key classical and contemporary experimental studies and findings in personality psychology

2: understand, relate and apply the key personality psychological concepts to daily life

3: conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during tutorial discussions, on personality psychology related topics

4: design, direct and regulate own study plan on personality psychology, from identifying the problem, setting learning objectives, researching on relevant information, reflecting on what has been learnt, to applying the knowledge to future problems

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Special Topics in Education and Human Development
courses.description: The instructor will direct the study of a topic in Education and Human Development in which he or she specializes.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000 or UGED2581
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Attain a deeper understanding of a specialized topic within Education and Human Development.

2. Develop the ability to assess the importance of research and/or applications of Education and Human Development in the pursuit of psychological wellbeing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Special Topics in Social and Industrial-Organizational Psychology
courses.description: The instructor will direct the study of a topic in Social and Industrial-Organizational Psychology in which he or she specializes.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000 or UGED2581
courses.learning_outcomes: The instructor will direct the study of a topic in Social and Industrial-Organizational Psychology in which he or she specializes.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Music
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to discuss and explore the psychological mechanisms involved in the perception, development, performance, and interpretation of music. These topics are approached via neurological, cognitive, developmental, and socio-cultural methods. Some of the topics include the perception of pitch and rhythm, musical structure, practice and the development of musical expertise, and the social dynamics in an ensemble. It is hoped that after taking this course students are able to analyze and discuss a range of musical phenomena and activities from a psychological point of view.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
(1) An understanding of the primary issues discussed in the contemporary study of psychology of music

(2) An understanding of the methods commonly used in the study of psychology of music

(3) An ability to discuss musical phenomena and activities from a psychological point of view

(4) Application of knowledge in psychology of music to music education, practice, and performance

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Machine Learning in Psychology

meetings.location: Lee Shau Kee Archi Bldg G02

courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of machine learning concepts and techniques, and their applications in psychology. Throughout the course, students will gain hands-on experience with various algorithms, such as supervised and unsupervised learning, techniques for feature selection, model evaluation, and the use of advanced methods such as neural networks and large language models. The course is designed to enable students to apply machine learning tools to psychological research, thereby fostering skills in data-driven hypothesis testing and research innovation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, you will be able to:

1. understand machine learning concepts, including different learning paradigms, algorithms, and the theoretical foundations underlying these methods.
2. develop and implement machine learning models, utilizing various techniques to analyze and interpret psychological data.
3. integrate machine learning methodologies with empirical psychological research to enhance data analysis, hypothesis testing, and the generation of new research questions.
4. communicate the rationale, process, and results of machine learning analyses in psychology to a diverse range of audiences.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Educational Psychology

meetings.location: Chung Chi College Lib CK TSE

courses.description: This course introduces the application of theoretical principles and research findings from the field of psychology to educational settings. Topics to be covered include general instructional issues, learning and motivation, effective instruction, educating students with special needs, measurement and evaluation. Special emphasis is placed on the understanding and solution of educational problems in the local community.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
Pre-requisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
Not for students who have taken EDUC3311.
courses.learning_outcomes:
I. Demonstrate a fundamental understanding in various concepts and theories of educational psychology
II. Be able to discuss and explain some principles governing learning from a psychological perspective
III. Be able to critically examine educational research and their implications
IV. Be able to analyse and discuss educational issues in an informative fashion

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology of Gender
courses.description: Gender affects people’s experiences, judgments and beliefs. This course reviews various perspectives on the psychology of gender. An analytical approach to understanding socialization, policies and cultures from a gendered perspective will be explored. Consequences of gender bias will be discussed. Upon completion of the course, students should demonstrate basic understanding of the major conceptual models of gender psychology and have better awareness of gender issues in different social and cultural contexts.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
I. Demonstrate a fundamental understanding in various concepts and theories of the psychology of gender

II. Be able to critically examine gender research and their implications

III. Be able to consider cultural, institutional, and media influences on the development of gender related beliefs and attitudes

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology

meetings.location: Chung Chi College Lib CK TSE
Chung Chi College Lib CK TSE
Chung Chi College Lib CK TSE

courses.description: Various types of psychological disorders falling under psychiatric nomenclature and other behavioural models. Theories and research concerning the origin, diagnosis and treatment of these disorders.
courses.enrollment_requirement:
Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
Not for students who have taken SOWK2140.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Learn the basic concepts of abnormal psychology.

2. Learn how brain predispositions and upbringing experience interact to lead to mental disorders.

3. Learn to do detailed clinical case analysis according to the integrative perspective.

4. Develop insights into your own and others’ mental processes.

5. Learn to use E-journals and internet in pursuing personal interests in this field.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of health psychology and the role of health psychologists in clinical and research settings. It examines biological, psychological, and social factors in the conceptions of health and health related attitudes, beliefs and behaviors. Topics include health promotion, behavioral health and illness prevention, substance abuse, stress and coping, management of chronic and terminal illness, pain management, and health services. Students will gain an understanding of the theory and everyday life applications of health psychology in contemporary societies.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. understand, relate and apply the key health psychological concepts to daily life

2. familiarize with the key classical and contemporary experimental studies and findings in health psychology

3. conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during tutorial discussions, on health psychology related topics

4. design, direct and regulate own study plan for problem-based learning, from identifying the problem, setting learning objectives, researching on relevant information, reflecting on what has been learnt, to applying the knowledge to future problems

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Professional Issues and Development in Mental Health Practice
courses.description: Issues of professional ethics, interdisciplinary approach and teamwork, professional development, and personal growth will be discussed with students as fundamentals in providing care to clients. A scientifically based psychosocial framework in conceptualizing and understanding individuals’ multi-faceted needs (physical and mental health, social and occupational needs) along with considerations of policy and structural issues to support individuals’ recovery will be discussed. Issues around diversity and mental health disparities are discussed to raise the consciousness of students.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Be familiar with the key concepts in mental health practice

2. Be able to weigh various perspectives underlying an ethical dilemma

3. Be aware of cultural diversity in mental health related issues

4. Be able to conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during in-class discussions, on mental health practice and related topics

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Evidence-based Mental Health Practice
courses.description: This course will introduce the essence of evidence-based practice and stepped care model in the delivery of mental health services. Students will understand how evidence is built around a certain intervention approach and/or for specific mental disorders. The issue of evidence will be discussed from multiple perspectives, from various quantitative approaches to establish efficacy and effectiveness to qualitative accounts from various stakeholders, including individuals with lived experience of mental health issues. Issues on the implementation and dissemination of evidence-based practice in real life settings will be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000 or UGED2581
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, you will be able to

a. Describe the basics of evidence-based practice and stepped care model in the delivery of mental health services

b. Describe the phenomena, cognitive-behavioral models, and interventions of common mental health problems

c. Demonstrate competence in quantitatively and qualitatively evaluating a treatment or intervention program.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Counseling Theories and their Applications to Clinical, Career and Organizational Settings

meetings.location: Chung Chi College Lib CK TSE

courses.description: This course will examine some common counseling theories and their usefulness in and applications in, various domains (clinical interventions, career counseling at schools, talent development by human resources). Coaching and some organizational development applications will be discussed and external speakers will provide an applied perspective on the field.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000 or UGED2581
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand the knowledge base of Counselling psychology

2. Develop critical thinking skills in Counselling psychology

3. Apply and relate Counselling psychology to interpersonal, career and organizational settings

4. Recognize the values in Counselling psychology

5. Gain effective communication skills

6. Gain insights about personal development in different contexts (school and organizational)

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Engagement and Assessment of Individuals with Common Mental Health Problems
courses.description: To effectively engage and assess individuals with common mental health difficulties, students will gain an understanding and competency in the application of “common factors” (e.g., active listening, rapport building, expression of empathy), knowledge in common mental health problems, and evidence-based interventions. The focus will be on training students on effective communication skills and assessment of individuals with anxiety and depression. Students will be trained on core skills of engagement, communication, and assessment through skills-based practices and role-plays. Students are expected to engage in self-practice self-reflection throughout the course by themselves or with their classmates. In order to qualify for practicum in guided self-help, students must pass the minimal competency requirements in conducting a complete assessment.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC3730 & PSYC3740
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, you will be able to

a. Describe the background knowledge pertinent to the three sections of an assessment including information gathering, information giving, and shared decision making.

b. Acquire micro skills to engage a client and develop a therapeutic alliance.

c. Demonstrate competence in conducting a collaborative assessment for the low-intensity psychological treatment program for common mental health problems.

d. Demonstrate competence in delivering an assessment using a range of methods including face-to-face, telephone, and electronic communication.

e. Reflect upon the process and outcome of clinical work in relation to theory and research evidence.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Evidence Based Low Intensity Interventions for Common Mental Health Problems
courses.description: Based on the evidence-based approaches for treatment of individuals with mild to moderate levels of common mental health problems, students will gain competency on a range of these evidence-based interventions, particularly low intensity cognitive behavioral interventions. Emphasis is put on clinical skills building to develop students’ “specific factors” competencies in the provision of low-intensity cognitive behavioral interventions using the guided self-help approach. Students will be trained on core skills of guided self-help through skills-based practices and role-plays. Students are expected to engage in self-practice self-reflection throughout the course by themselves or with their classmates. In order to qualify for practicum in guided self-help, students must pass the minimal competency requirements in conducting a complete intervention using the guided self-help approach.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC3760
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, you will be able to

a. Demonstrate competence in planning a collaborative low-intensity psychological treatment programme for common mental health problems

b. Describe a range of evidence-based interventions and strategies to assist patients to manage their emotional distress and disturbance

c. Evaluate and use competently low-intensity basic, intervention-specific and problem-specific techniques such as behavioural activation, exposure, guided problem solving, and dealing with worry, according to individualised assessment and theoretical basis

d. Demonstrate competence in delivering low-intensity interventions using a range of methods including face-to-face, telephone and electronic communication

e. Evaluate the role of case management and stepped-care approaches to managing common mental health problems in primary care, including ongoing risk management appropriate to service protocols

f. Reflect upon the processes and outcome of clinical work in relation to theory and research evidence

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Applied Psychology in Business
courses.description: The course covers the application of psychological knowledge in service and industrial operations. Topics include the psychological foundation of consumer behaviour and advertising, the psychological analysis of the interaction between sales personnel and customers, economic psychology, current motivational techniques for enhancing performance, team-building, the psychology of industrial relations, and other current topics. The course will give equal emphasis to theories and applications.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGEC2581 or UGED2581.
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. understand, relate and apply key I/O Psychology concepts to work life

2. become familiar with some of the important studies and experimental findings in I/O Psychology

3. conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both on tests and during tutorial discussions, on Psychology-related topics

4. design, direct and regulate own study plan for problem-based learning, from identifying the problem to setting learning objectives and applying knowledge to future problems

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychology in Action I
courses.description:
This course helps students to apply psychology to tackle social issues. Students will learn about successful stories of psychology applications, and under the guidance of the teaching team, design and implement their own projects in an attempt to apply theories and findings of psychology to make an impact on people's lives and the society-at-large.
A problem-based learning approach will be implemented in this course. Under the framework of design thinking, students will identify the issue of interest and apply their psychological knowledge to create changes on the issues. Students will be engaged in a wide range of in-class discussions, problem-based activities, and self-reflection processes to facilitate their learning. Students are expected to go outside the classroom, connect with the potential stakeholders and discuss their proposal with them. By the end of the course, students are required to give a group presentation and submit a project proposal to consolidate their thinking and efforts and to reflect on the possibility of future actions.

Advisory: For Psychology Majors only.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Pre-requisite(s): PSYC1000 or UGED2581

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Practicum in Education and Human Development
courses.description:
This course introduces students to applied developmental settings such as schools, organizations that work with children and adolescents, and medical institutions such that they will have an opportunity to apply the theories and subject matter of developmental and educational psychology in the "real world". Students will arrange a practicum placement together with the course lecturer.

Advisory: For Psychology Majors only.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGED2581, PSYC2530 or 2540 or 3540 or 3550, and permission of course teacher.
courses.course_attributes:
Capstone Course
Experiential Learning Course
Internship
courses.learning_outcomes:
Students will:
1. Refresh, deepen, and broaden their understanding of concepts, theoretical perspectives, and empirical findings in educational and/or developmental psychology that are relevant to observations made and tasks/projects worked on at the placement site.
2. Apply their understanding of theory and research in psychology in general and educational and/or developmental psychology in particular to personal, organizational, and social issues.
3. Recognize and appreciate socio-cultural complexity and diversity.
4. Develop insights into their own and others’ behavior and psyche and employ effective strategies for self-management and self-improvement.
5. Emerge from the course with realistic ideas about how to implement their knowledge, skills, and values in psychology in a variety of applied settings.
6. Communicate effectively in a variety of formats.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Practicum in Psychology and Health
courses.description:
This course focuses on training students in the application of theories and practice related to clinical and health psychology across social welfare, health, and other applied settings in the community. Students will be assigned a practicum placement by the course instructor.

Advisory: For Psychology Majors only.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: PSYC1000 or UGED2581, PSYC2780 or 3700 or 3720 or 3730 or 3740, and permission of course teacher.
courses.course_attributes:
Capstone Course
Experiential Learning Course
Internship
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. understand, relate, and apply the key psychological concepts in applied settings
2. gain hands-on experience in applied settings
3. conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during weekly discussions, on health/clinical psychology-related topics
4. design, direct, and regulate one’s work plan, from generating original ideas, listing of possible plans, setting expected work outcomes, researching on relevant information, reflecting on what have been learned, to applying the knowledge in future encounter at applied settings

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Practicum
courses.description:
This course introduces students to research through working in one of the research centres or laboratories to conduct psychology studies in a scientific manner that they will have an opportunity to apply psychology research methods. courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Undergraduate Practicum in Guided Self-Help
courses.description: Students will provide guided self-help services in community settings under the supervision of clinical psychologists. This practicum experience represents the culmination of knowledge and competencies that the students have developed towards assessment of common mental health difficulties and interventions using low-intensity interventions and guided self-help within the stepped care model. Students at the practicum settings will work as part of the team in providing evidence-based services to individuals with mild to moderate common mental health difficulties. Issues pertinent to service delivery such as risk management, medication, and multi-cultural competence are discussed to raise the awareness, sensitivity, and competence of students in providing services. The science and practice of adaptations during the service implementation to accommodate individuals from diverse social, cultural, health, economic, and occupational backgrounds as well as in-service settings with varied resources and community contexts will be introduced to enhance students’ critical appreciation of the knowledge, attitudes, and competencies required to support clients’ recovery in an inclusive, value-driven way. Students need to fulfill at least 160 hours on-site under the supervision of clinical psychologists and attend biweekly one-hour clinical skills supervision by the course instructor.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Seminar in Research Methods I
courses.description: This course helps students to understand the concepts and methods of data analysis in social research. In particular, students will learn how to apply appropriate statistical methods in various research scenarios and how to interpret the results. The usage of statistical packages such as SPSS will be covered. Even though mathematical proofs and statistical derivations will be reduced to a minimum, having the knowledge of basic mathematics and matrix manipulations will be helpful.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Ind-Organizational Psychology or MPhil-PhD Psychology or MSSc Clinical Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes: Upon completion of this course, you will have a better understanding about the concepts and principles of statistical modeling and data analysis in general. Moreover, you should be more proficient in applying different statistical techniques such as correlation and multiple regression analysis, logistic regression, ANCOVA and MANOVA.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Research Methods
courses.description: This course helps students to understand the concepts and methods of quantitative and qualitative data analysis in social research. In particular, students will learn how to apply appropriate statistical methods in various research scenarios and how to interpret the results. The usage of statistical packages such as R and SPSS will be covered. Basic knowledge in statistical methods is a pre-requirement.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Ind-Organizational Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to:
1. Demonstrate a fundamental understanding of the key concepts, principles, and procedures of statistical analyses commonly used in Industrial and Organizational Psychology.
2. Select and apply appropriate statistical procedures to test research hypotheses, and interpret statistical results presented in the scientific literature.
3. Differentiate among and evaluate basic types of experimental, quasi-experimental, and non-experimental research designs.
4. Analyze quantitative data, interpret multivariate statistical results, and communicate research findings effectively in both scientific and business settings.
5. Critically evaluate the strengths and limitations of various analytic tools and research designs in applied psychological research.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Statistics and Research Design in Psychological Science
courses.description: In this course students will learn to understand the logic, purpose and techniques of statistical analyses, particularly those for psychology, and learn the basic types of experimental designs (e.g., within-subjects designs vs. between-subjects designs) and know how to use them appropriately in various situations. Students will also learn to address the important issues in designing and conducting psychological experiments (e.g., Research ethics, Literature review, Control groups, Presentations). We will emphasize the understanding of logic and attempt to reduce load of memory.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Students will know the procedure to carry out statistical methods in psychology and be able to both use them in practical question and understand them in the scientific literature.
2. Students will understand the logic behind those procedures and know how to solve similar questions.
3. Students will know the basic types of experimental designs (e.g., within-subjects designs vs. between-subjects designs) and know how to use them appropriately in various situations.
4. Students will know how to address the important issues in designing and conducting psychological experiments (e.g., Research ethics, Literature review, Control groups, Presentations).

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Psychological Testing and Measurement
courses.description: This course is designed to cover the basic principles of psychological measurement and the techniques of test construction, administration, and validation.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Able to understand the basic concepts and principles of psychological measurement.
2. Able to evaluate the quality of a psychological test scientifically.
3. Able to constract a test with desirable psychometric properties.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Capstone Project
courses.description: In this capstone course, students will work in small groups to address an applied psychology topic that will utilize their skills and knowledge in psychology. Under the supervision of the course instructor, students will identify a social issue, conduct literature research to design an intervention to address the issue, carry out the intervention, and assess the effectiveness of the intervention. Students will document their process in an applied research report. At the completion of the course, students should be able to learn how to apply psychological knowledge and skills in addressing social issues.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Psychology programme

| Critically analyze social issues from a psychological perspective | |
| Formulate interventions based on psychological research | |
| Systematically assess effectiveness of a psychological intervention | |
| Communicate succinctly in verbally and in writing psychology concepts and theories | |

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Health Psychology
courses.description: This course provides an overview of health psychology and the role of health psychologists in clinical and research settings. It examines biological, psychological, and social factors in the conceptions of health and health related attitudes, beliefs and behaviors. Topics include health promotion, behavioral health and illness prevention, substance abuse, stress and coping, management of chronic and terminal illness, pain management, and health services. Students will gain an understanding of the theory and everyday life applications of health psychology in contemporary societies.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Educational Psychology
courses.description: This course introduces the application of theoretical principles and research findings from the field of psychology to educational settings. Topics to be covered include general instructional issues, learning and motivation, effective instruction, educating students with special needs, measurement and evaluation. Special emphasis is placed on the understanding and solution of educational problems in the local community.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Psychology Programme
courses.learning_outcomes:
I. Demonstrate a fundamental understanding in various concepts and theories of educational psychology
II. Be able to discuss and explain some principles governing learning from a psychological perspective
III. Be able to critically examine educational research and their implications
IV. Be able to analyse and discuss educational issues in an informative fashion

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Industrial-organizational Psychology
courses.description: Work is an indispensable part of life. And the study of psychology at work is a domain of Industrial/ Organizational (I/O) psychology. This course focuses on the application of psychological methods and principles in understanding the world of work and work behaviors.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Psychology programme
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Be knowledgeable of the topics, methodologies, essential concepts and findings in Industrial-organizational Psychology

2. Be able to reflect upon work related issues from a psychological perspective

3. Be able to recognize the values in industrial-organizational psychology

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Biological Psychology
courses.description: This course addresses brain-behavior relationships. Emphasis will, therefore, be on the basic concepts of how the nervous system and the brain works in explanation for the behaviors, emotions and thoughts of human beings. The significance of studying and applying the neuropsychological concepts in daily life will be highlighted. It will also introduce some abnormal cognitive and emotional problems in relation to the malfunction of the brain.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. To have basic understanding of some major concepts, theoretical perspectives and empirical findings in physiological psychology and neuropsychology.
2. To apply some basic neuropsychological principles to daily life experience, such as knowledge of brain function enhancing activities; precautions in encountering people suffering from brain disorders.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Cognitive Psychology
courses.description: This course aims at inspiring students to consider the question of how human being can dominate the earth from the perspective of cognitive psychology. Throughout the evolutionary history, our ancestors developed a repertoire of cognitive skills that are fundamental to human civilization. In some cases, we are different from other animals quantitatively (e.g., capacity of memory). In other cases, the ability concerned may be unique to us (e.g., communication with language). It is indeed difficult to imagine a life without these cognitive abilities. In lectures, students will be introduced with the basic concepts and findings about various cognitive abilities including cognition, sensation, perception, memory system, decision-making, and language-processing. In tutorials, they will receive trainings in conducting research in cognitive psychology.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand, relate and apply the key concepts of cognitive psychology to daily life.
2. Familiarize with the key classical and contemporary experimental studies and findings in cognitive psychology.
3. Conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during tutorial discussions, on topics related to cognitive psychology.
4. Design, direct and regulate own study plan for problem-based learning, from identifying the problem, setting learning objectives, researching on relevant information, reflecting on what has been learnt, to applying the knowledge to future problems.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Developmental Psychology
courses.description: The goal of this course is to introduce students to the field of developmental psychology. We will explore theories, research methods, and research findings on physical, cognitive, and psychosocial development from early childhood to old age. We will also pay attention to the role of culture in shaping life-span development.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Acquire a broad overview of life-span development
2. Understand and apply major concepts and research findings in developmental psychology to everyday life
3. Cultivate awareness of diversity and critical thinking through analyzing real-life issues in relation to developmental psychology
4. Promote personal growth through reflecting on one’s own development

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Social Psychology
courses.description: This course provides a broad survey of the field of social psychology. After reviewing key theoretical and methodological approaches in the field, students will be exposed to different topic areas in social psychology, such as the self, group processes, interpersonal relationship, social influence, social cognition, aggression, and altruism. The course also incorporates cross-cultural perspective in discussing these topics.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Understand key ideas and research findings in social psychology
2. Understand how research in social psychology is carried out
3. Apply theories and methods of social psychology in everyday life
4. Clearly communicate issues relevant to social psychology

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Abnormal Psychology
courses.description: Dramatic advances have occurred in the past two decades in the study of psychopathology. Human genome has been fully sequenced, the technologies of neuroimaging have made it possible for researchers to observe a brain in action in living people, and psychology has entered the Decade of the Mind. In this new decade, psychology has been re-defined as a science examining how human mind works in general. Abnormal psychology, on the other hand, specializes in understanding how human mind works when it goes haywire. This course is designed to provide you with the most updated knowledge in the field of psychopathology. You will learn about the key concepts of mental disorders, how mental predispositions and upbringing experience interact in the development of various mental disorders, how human mind works in different mental disorders, and more importantly, how you can continue to learn about the science of psychopathology on your own after you have completed the course. After all, learning is about “learning how to learn.”
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1. Familiarize with the DSM system for classifying and diagnosing different mental disorders.
2. Understand the development of different mental disorders.
3. Apply what have learnt in this course in analyzing real clinical cases.
4. Pursue own study interests and develop own study topics in abnormal psychology.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Personality Psychology
courses.description: This course presents the major theoretical approaches to personality and the basic techniques utilized to assess personality differences. The focus is on everyday life applications, empirical evidence in support and against the theories, and the design, application, and interpretation of personality questionnaires.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
1: familiarize with the key classical and contemporary experimental studies and findings in personality psychology
2: understand, relate and apply the key personality psychological concepts to daily life
3: conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during tutorial discussions, on personality psychology related topics
4: design, direct and regulate own study plan on personality psychology, from identifying the problem, setting learning objectives, researching on relevant information, reflecting on what has been learnt, to applying the knowledge to future problems

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Independent Study
courses.description: This course is an application of the student-oriented method of teaching to psychological research. Students will conduct an empirical research study on an approved topic under intensive supervision of a teacher. Students, on an individual basis, are expected to conduct literature review to identify research hypotheses, design a research study, collect, and analyse the data, and write up a publishable research report. Upon successful completion of the independent study, students will be able to master the basic skills to conduct a psychology research study.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MA in Psychology programme
courses.learning_outcomes:
Independent Study in Cognitive Science:

1. Enhance critical thinking skills in psychology
2. Apply scientific methods in psychology to research

Independent Study in Human Development:

1. Be able to conceptualize research questions and formulate specific hypotheses in the study of human development
2. Be familiarized with writing research reports
3. Be able to apply the research knowledge and techniques to both academic and applied settings

Independent Study in Social Psychology:

1. Students will be able to transform a conceptual idea to a testable research question in the field of social psychology
2. Students will be able to draw evidence-based conclusions and inferences in the research field of social psychology by conducting systematic and scientific analyses
3. The research skills learned in the course will be applicable to both academic research and applied settings (e.g., educational institutions) in particular to organizational studies and community research

Independent Study in Mental Health:

1. Students will be able to conceptualize research questions and establish testable hypotheses in the studies of mental health
2. Students will be able to apply different research methods in studying mental health issues
3. Students will be familiarized with academic writing and presentation
4. Students will be able to apply the research skills to both academic research and applied settings, including community health studies and mental health promotion

References will be made to the most current international perspectives and codes of professional conduct to inform our understanding of best practices as scientist-practitioners. courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Neuropsychology Assessment
courses.description: This seminar addresses the application of neuropsychology for clinical assessment. Emphasis will be on the examination of the effects of CNS on the behaviours of individuals and the cognitive disorders associated with various brain disorders. Several widely used instruments (i.e., tests and test battery) which measure a variety of neuropsychological disorders will be discussed.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Clinical Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to:
1. acquire fundamental understanding of some basic but important concepts and theories in clinical neuropsychology,
2. learn about the value and application of clinical neuropsychological assessment,
3. learn about the neuropsychological tests for Chinese population,
4. acquire the basic concept on results interpretation and report writing.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Writing and Presentation
courses.description: This course will explore various types of writing as well as techniques to maximize effectiveness in oral presentations essential for psychology for graduate students. Topics to be covered include how to write thesis proposals, grant proposals, empirical studies, manuscript reviews, and review articles. We will also explore techniques for effective critiquing of manuscripts, writing clearly and concisely, understanding and incorporating APA style, and avoiding plagiarism. In addition, oral presentation skills will be overviewed, with opportunities for all students to practice presenting their own research.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Ind-Organizational Psychology or MPhil-PhD Psychology or PhD Clinical Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students will be expected to:
- acquire the basic rules and skill in writing and presentation in psychology
- effectively assess and distinguish journal papers and other works in psychology
- grasp the writing and presentation skills and use these skills in the research career

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Professional Attitude, Demeanor, and Identity of Clinical Psychologists I
courses.description: This course aims to enhance students’ professional attitude, values, and identity as they begin the journey of becoming clinical psychologists. Timed with Clinical Placements I-II of the MSSc Programme, the course content covers a wide range of topics encompassing service setup and organisation, work ethos and professional demeanor, handling caseload and paperwork, seeking and learning from feedback, managing professional relationships, and self-care.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Clinical Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to:
1. Formulate a well-informed understanding of the role of clinical psychologists in the design and delivery of professional services, within the broader context of multidisciplinary teams and organisational structures
2. Recognise and uphold the importance of professional attitudes, values, and priorities in clinical psychological practice
3. Demonstrate a commitment to professional excellence through continuous self-improvement in competencies, professional demeanor, and ethical conduct
4. Reflect critically on supervisory experiences and identify strategies to enhance the productivity, effectiveness, and collaborative nature of clinical supervision

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Applied Research I
courses.description: This course provides students with applied research skills in conducting research within workplace settings. Emphasizing real-world applications, it covers advanced research design, data analysis, and interpretation. Students will learn to address organizational issues through evidence-based research while considering ethical implications, preparing them to contribute effectively as researchers in the field of I-O psychology.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Ind-Organizational Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to:
1. Design and implement advanced research studies in organizational contexts

2. Analyze and interpret organizational data using appropriate statistical and methodological tools

3. Apply ethical principles and evidence-based reasoning to address organizational challenges

courses.description: This course is a continuation of PSYC6510 Applied Research I, which allows students to build upon and to extend the breadth and depth of their project in PSYC6511.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Ind-Organizational Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to:
1. Design and implement advanced research studies in organizational contexts

2. Analyze and interpret organizational data using appropriate statistical and methodological tools

3. Apply ethical principles and evidence-based reasoning to address organizational challenges

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Engagement and Motivation in Organizations
courses.description: This is the first course of a series of two courses in organizational psychology. Topics covered in this course include: job attitudes, work motivation, stress, job enrichment, communication, decision making, and conflict management.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Ind-Organizational Psychology or MSSc Ind-Organizational Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to:
1. Critically review and consolidate theories and empirical findings in organizational psychology at an individual level (e.g., employee
engagement, motivation, citizenship behaviors, stress and counter-productive work behaviors), a group level (e.g., team
composition/diversity, mental models, group decision making and leadership) and an organizational level (e.g., organizational
culture and organizational learning).
2. Critically evaluate and develop independent views on theories and empirical findings in organizational psychology at individual,
group and organizational levels.
3. Make informed judgments on how theories and empirical findings in organizational psychology could be applied in work settings.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Leadership and Group Dynamics
courses.description: This is the second course of a series of two courses in organizational psychology that provides a critical review of interpersonal, group, and organizational level issues in organizations. Topics covered include: groups dynamics, leadership and management, organizational development, and cross-cultural issues in organizational psychology.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Ind-Organizational Psychology or MSSc Ind-Organizational Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this course, students are expected to:
1. Critically review and consolidate theories and empirical findings in organizational psychology at an individual level (e.g., citizenship behaviors, and counter-productive work behaviors), a group level (e.g., team composition/diversity, mental models, group decision making and leadership) and an organizational level (e.g., organizational culture and organizational learning).
2. Critically evaluate and develop independent views on theories and empirical findings in organizational psychology at individual, group and organizational levels.
3. Make informed judgments on how theories and empirical findings in organizational psychology could be applied in work settings.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Organizational Placement III
courses.description: Students will be placed to major organizations for internship training for 500 hours. They will work on a specific project in the organization under the joint supervision of a field supervisor of the host organization and a teacher from the Division.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MPhil-PhD Ind-Organizational Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this practicum, students are expected to:
1. acquire major concepts and theoretical perspectives in IO psychology
2. apply theoretical perspectives in IO psychology to personal, social, and organizational issues
3. develop critical thinking skills to make reflection on other values that are the underpinnings of psychology as a discipline
4. conceptualize, structure, articulate and present original ideas, both in written assignments and during discussions,
on IO psychology-related topics
5. develop positive values on respecting the complexity of sociocultural diversity develop self-management skills by means
of applying effective strategies for self-improvement attain personal growth through engaging in the practicum with
realistic ideas about how to implement the psychological knowledge, skills, and values in a variety of applied settings

courses.enrollment_requirement: For students in MSSc Ind-Organizational Psychology
courses.learning_outcomes:
Upon completion of this practicum, students are expected to:
1. Apply theoretical knowledge to real-world organizational challenges

2. Collaborate effectively with professionals in organizational environments

3. Reflect critically on professional experiences to enhance I-O psychology competencies
